import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture

A conjectured local–global principle for linear ordinary differential equations: a linear
differential system $dY/dz = A(z)\,Y$ with $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$ has a full set of algebraic
solutions as soon as, for all but finitely many primes $p$, its reduction modulo $p$ has
$p$-curvature zero (equivalently, has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$).

The $p$-curvature is computed by the recurrence $A_0 = I$, $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$ (so that
$d^kY/dz^k = A_k Y$ for every solution $Y$): the $p$-curvature of the reduction modulo $p$ vanishes
if and only if $A_p \equiv 0 \pmod p$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck%E2%80%93Katz_p-curvature_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. Chambert-Loir, *Théorèmes d'algébrisation en géométrie diophantienne*, Séminaire Bourbaki
  Exp. 886, §3, [arXiv:math/0103192](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103192)
- N. M. Katz, *Algebraic solutions of differential equations ($p$-curvature and the Hodge
  filtration)*, Invent. Math. 18 (1972), 1–118
- N. M. Katz, *A conjecture in the arithmetic theory of differential equations*, Bull. Soc. Math.
  France 110 (1982), 203–239
- L. Di Vizio, *Arithmetic theory of $q$-difference equations*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002),
  [arXiv:math/0104178](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0104178)
-/
namespace GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture
open Polynomial RatFunc
open scoped Differential

/- ### The differential field `K(X)`

Mathlib has no derivation on `RatFunc K`. We define `d/dX` by the quotient rule on the reduced
numerator and denominator and record it as a `Differential` instance, so that the unique extension
of `d/dX` to finite extensions of `K(X)` (`Differential.differentialFiniteDimensional`) is
available. -/
section RatFuncDerivative
variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivative (r : RatFunc K) : RatFunc K :=
  (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative r.num) * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.denom -
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.num * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative r.denom)) /
    algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.denom ^ 2
blocks.docstring:
The derivative `d/dX` of a rational function `r = f / g` (with `f = r.num`, `g = r.denom`),
given by the quotient rule `(f' g - f g') / g ^ 2`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Polynomial.derivative / Polynomial.derivative' (only on K[X]); LaurentSeries.derivative (a linear map, not a Derivation, and not on RatFunc); KaehlerDifferential.D (universal derivation, would require identifying Ω[ℚ(z)/ℚ] with ℚ(z)); Mathlib.FieldTheory.Differential.Basic (extends a derivation to finite extensions, but needs a Differential instance on the base field).
justification.name: GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture.ratFuncDerivative (+ ratFuncDerivativeAddHom, instance Differential (RatFunc K))
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no derivation d/dX on RatFunc K, and the conjecture needs both the higher derivative matrices A_k over ℚ(z) and a `Differential` instance on ℚ(z) so that Mathlib's unique extension of the derivation to finite extensions becomes available. Defined by the quotient rule on num/denom and proven (no sorry) to be a derivation agreeing with Polynomial.derivative on polynomials.

blocks.name: ratFuncDerivative
blocks.text:
/-- The derivative `d/dX` of a rational function `r = f / g` (with `f = r.num`, `g = r.denom`),
given by the quotient rule `(f' g - f g') / g ^ 2`. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivative (r : RatFunc K) : RatFunc K :=
  (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative r.num) * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.denom -
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.num * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative r.denom)) /
    algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.denom ^ 2

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem ratFuncDerivative_div (p q : K[X]) (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    ratFuncDerivative (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q) =
      (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative p) * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q -
          algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative q)) /
        algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q ^ 2 := by
  set r := algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q with hr
  have h1 : r.num * q = p * r.denom := (num_mul_eq_mul_denom_iff hq).mpr hr
  have h2 : derivative r.num * q + r.num * derivative q =
      derivative p * r.denom + p * derivative r.denom := by
    simpa only [derivative_mul] using congrArg derivative h1
  have key : (derivative r.num * r.denom - r.num * derivative r.denom) * q ^ 2 =
      (derivative p * q - p * derivative q) * r.denom ^ 2 := by
    linear_combination (r.denom * q) * h2 - (derivative q * r.denom + derivative r.denom * q) * h1
  unfold ratFuncDerivative
  rw [div_eq_div_iff (pow_ne_zero 2 (algebraMap_ne_zero (denom_ne_zero r)))
    (pow_ne_zero 2 (algebraMap_ne_zero hq))]
  simpa only [map_mul, map_sub, map_pow] using congrArg (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)) key
blocks.docstring:
The quotient rule holds for any representation `p / q` of a rational function, not only for
the reduced one.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem ratFuncDerivative_add (x y : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncDerivative (x + y) = ratFuncDerivative x + ratFuncDerivative y := by
  induction x using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₁ q₁ hq₁ => ?_
  induction y using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₂ q₂ hq₂ => ?_
  rw [div_add_div _ _ (algebraMap_ne_zero hq₁) (algebraMap_ne_zero hq₂), ← map_mul,
    ← map_mul, ← map_add, ← map_mul, ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ (mul_ne_zero hq₁ hq₂),
    ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₁, ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₂]
  have h₁ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₁
  have h₂ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₂
  simp only [derivative_mul, map_add, map_mul]
  field_simp
  ring

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem ratFuncDerivative_mul (x y : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncDerivative (x * y) = x * ratFuncDerivative y + y * ratFuncDerivative x := by
  induction x using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₁ q₁ hq₁ => ?_
  induction y using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₂ q₂ hq₂ => ?_
  rw [div_mul_div_comm, ← map_mul, ← map_mul,
    ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ (mul_ne_zero hq₁ hq₂), ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₁,
    ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₂]
  have h₁ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₁
  have h₂ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₂
  simp only [derivative_mul, map_add, map_mul]
  field_simp
  ring

noncomputable def ratFuncDerivativeAddHom : RatFunc K →+ RatFunc K :=
  AddMonoidHom.mk' ratFuncDerivative ratFuncDerivative_add

blocks.name: ratFuncDerivativeAddHom
blocks.text:
/-- `ratFuncDerivative` as an additive map. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivativeAddHom : RatFunc K →+ RatFunc K :=
  AddMonoidHom.mk' ratFuncDerivative ratFuncDerivative_add

  deriv := @Derivation.mk' ℤ _ (RatFunc K) _ (Ring.toIntAlgebra _) (RatFunc K) _ _ _
    (ratFuncDerivativeAddHom (K := K)).toIntLinearMap ratFuncDerivative_mul

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem deriv_algebraMap_polynomial (f : K[X]) :
    (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) f)′ = algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative f) := by
  change ratFuncDerivative _ = _
  simpa using ratFuncDerivative_div f 1 one_ne_zero
blocks.docstring: On polynomials, the derivation of `K(X)` is the usual polynomial derivative.
blocks.name: deriv_algebraMap_polynomial
blocks.text:
/-- On polynomials, the derivation of `K(X)` is the usual polynomial derivative. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem deriv_algebraMap_polynomial (f : K[X]) :
    (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) f)′ = algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative f) := by
  change ratFuncDerivative _ = _
  simpa using ratFuncDerivative_div f 1 one_ne_zero

theorem deriv_X : (X : RatFunc K)′ = 1 := by
  rw [← algebraMap_X, deriv_algebraMap_polynomial, derivative_X, map_one]

/- ### The matrices `A_k` and the `p`-curvature -/
section HigherDerivMatrix

blocks.command_arg: {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Differential R] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
blocks.text: variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Differential R] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def higherDerivMatrix (A : Matrix ι ι R) : ℕ → Matrix ι ι R
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => (higherDerivMatrix A k).map (·′) + higherDerivMatrix A k * A
blocks.docstring:
For a matrix `A` over a differential ring, `higherDerivMatrix A k` is the matrix `A_k` defined
by the recurrence `A_0 = 1`, `A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A` (where `A_k'` is the entrywise derivative),
so that every solution `Y` of `Y' = A Y` satisfies `Y^{(k)} = A_k Y`.

For `A` over `ℚ(z)` and a prime `p`, the reduction modulo `p` of `A_p` is the `p`-curvature of
the reduction modulo `p` of the system `Y' = A Y`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Matrix.map with Differential.deriv (used inside the recursion); no p-curvature or iterated-derivative-matrix notion exists.
justification.name: GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture.higherDerivMatrix
justification.why_needed: The p-curvature matrix A_p of Chambert-Loir: A_0 = 1, A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A over any differential commutative ring; no analogue exists in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: higherDerivMatrix
blocks.text:
/-- For a matrix `A` over a differential ring, `higherDerivMatrix A k` is the matrix `A_k` defined
by the recurrence `A_0 = 1`, `A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A` (where `A_k'` is the entrywise derivative),
so that every solution `Y` of `Y' = A Y` satisfies `Y^{(k)} = A_k Y`.

For `A` over `ℚ(z)` and a prime `p`, the reduction modulo `p` of `A_p` is the `p`-curvature of
the reduction modulo `p` of the system `Y' = A Y`. -/
noncomputable def higherDerivMatrix (A : Matrix ι ι R) : ℕ → Matrix ι ι R
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => (higherDerivMatrix A k).map (·′) + higherDerivMatrix A k * A

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem higherDerivMatrix_zero (A : Matrix ι ι R) : higherDerivMatrix A 0 = 1 := rfl

theorem higherDerivMatrix_zero (A : Matrix ι ι R) : higherDerivMatrix A 0 = 1 := rfl

theorem higherDerivMatrix_succ (A : Matrix ι ι R) (k : ℕ) :
    higherDerivMatrix A (k + 1) =
      (higherDerivMatrix A k).map (·′) + higherDerivMatrix A k * A := rfl

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem higherDerivMatrix_one (A : Matrix ι ι R) : higherDerivMatrix A 1 = A := by
  have : (1 : Matrix ι ι R).map (·′) = 0 := by
    ext i j
    by_cases h : i = j <;> simp [h]
  simp [higherDerivMatrix, this]

/- ### Reduction modulo `p` of rational functions over `ℚ` -/
section ReductionModP

blocks.code:
def IsPIntegral (p : ℕ) (r : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f g : ℤ[X], g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    r = algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (f.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) /
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))
blocks.docstring:
A rational function `r ∈ ℚ(z)` is *`p`-integral* (its reduction modulo `p` is defined) if
`r = f / g` with `f, g ∈ ℤ[z]` and `g ≢ 0 (mod p)`. Equivalently, `r` has `p`-adic Gauss norm
at most `1`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Polynomial.gaussNorm (takes an AbsoluteValue into ℝ and would need a p-adic absolute value on ℚ plus a quotient for RatFunc); padicNorm (on ℚ only); Valuation subrings / IsLocalization at pℤ[X] (much heavier and no ready-made map to RatFunc ℚ).
justification.name: GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture.IsPIntegral
justification.why_needed: Encodes 'r ∈ ℚ(z) can be reduced modulo p' (p-adic Gauss norm ≤ 1): r = f/g with f, g ∈ ℤ[z], g ≢ 0 mod p.

blocks.name: IsPIntegral
blocks.text:
/-- A rational function `r ∈ ℚ(z)` is *`p`-integral* (its reduction modulo `p` is defined) if
`r = f / g` with `f, g ∈ ℤ[z]` and `g ≢ 0 (mod p)`. Equivalently, `r` has `p`-adic Gauss norm
at most `1`. -/
def IsPIntegral (p : ℕ) (r : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f g : ℤ[X], g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    r = algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (f.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) /
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))

blocks.code:
def IsZeroModP (p : ℕ) (r : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f g : ℤ[X], g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    f.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = 0 ∧
    r = algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (f.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) /
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))
blocks.docstring:
A rational function `r ∈ ℚ(z)` is *zero modulo `p`* if `r = f / g` with `f, g ∈ ℤ[z]`,
`g ≢ 0 (mod p)` and `f ≡ 0 (mod p)`. Equivalently, `r` has `p`-adic Gauss norm less than `1`,
i.e. `r` is `p`-integral and its reduction in `𝔽_p(z)` is `0`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Same as for IsPIntegral; no reduction map ℚ(z) ⊇ ℤ_(p)(z) → 𝔽_p(z) exists in Mathlib.
justification.name: GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture.IsZeroModP
justification.why_needed: Encodes 'r ≡ 0 mod p' for r ∈ ℚ(z) (Gauss norm < 1): r = f/g with f ≡ 0 mod p, g ≢ 0 mod p; used to say the p-curvature matrix vanishes mod p.

blocks.name: IsZeroModP
blocks.text:
/-- A rational function `r ∈ ℚ(z)` is *zero modulo `p`* if `r = f / g` with `f, g ∈ ℤ[z]`,
`g ≢ 0 (mod p)` and `f ≡ 0 (mod p)`. Equivalently, `r` has `p`-adic Gauss norm less than `1`,
i.e. `r` is `p`-integral and its reduction in `𝔽_p(z)` is `0`. -/
def IsZeroModP (p : ℕ) (r : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f g : ℤ[X], g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    f.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = 0 ∧
    r = algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (f.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) /
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem isZeroModP_zero (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : IsZeroModP p 0 :=
  ⟨0, 1, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩
blocks.name: isZeroModP_zero
blocks.text:
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem isZeroModP_zero (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : IsZeroModP p 0 :=
  ⟨0, 1, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_isZeroModP_one (p : ℕ) : ¬ IsZeroModP p 1 := by
  rintro ⟨f, g, hg, hf, h⟩
  have hg' : g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    rintro hg'
    simp [hg'] at h
  rw [eq_div_iff (algebraMap_ne_zero hg'), one_mul] at h
  have hfg : f = g := Polynomial.map_injective _ (Int.castRingHom ℚ).injective_int
    (algebraMap_injective ℚ h).symm
  exact hg (hfg ▸ hf)
blocks.name: not_isZeroModP_one
blocks.text:
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_isZeroModP_one (p : ℕ) : ¬ IsZeroModP p 1 := by
  rintro ⟨f, g, hg, hf, h⟩
  have hg' : g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    rintro hg'
    simp [hg'] at h
  rw [eq_div_iff (algebraMap_ne_zero hg'), one_mul] at h
  have hfg : f = g := Polynomial.map_injective _ (Int.castRingHom ℚ).injective_int
    (algebraMap_injective ℚ h).symm
  exact hg (hfg ▸ hf)

def HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : IntermediateField F (AlgebraicClosure F)) (_ : FiniteDimensional F L)
    (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L),

The linear differential system `Y' = A Y`, for `A` an `n × n` matrix over a differential
field `F` of characteristic `0`, has a *full set of algebraic solutions*: there is a fundamental
matrix of solutions, i.e. an invertible `n × n` matrix `Y` with `Y' = A Y`, whose entries lie in
a finite extension `L` of `F` (inside an algebraic closure of `F`). Here `L` carries the unique
derivation extending that of `F`.

blocks.docstring:
**Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture** (Grothendieck's conjecture, in its essential
case). Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix of rational functions in $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, and consider
the linear differential system $dY/dz = A(z)\,Y$. Let $A_0 = I$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$, so
that $d^kY/dz^k = A_k Y$ for every solution $Y$.

Suppose that for all but finitely many primes $p$, the system can be reduced modulo $p$ and the
reduced system has $p$-curvature zero, i.e. $A_p \equiv 0 \pmod p$ (equivalently, the reduced
system has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$, or algebraic over $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$).
Then the system has a full set of algebraic solutions: a fundamental matrix
$Y \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ with $Y' = AY$, whose entries lie in a finite extension $L$ of
$\mathbb{Q}(z)$.

Only this sufficiency direction is conjectural; the converse (necessity of the mod $p$ condition)
is a classical theorem of Cartier and Katz.

theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture {n : ℕ}

claims.decomposer_note: Primary conjecture in the article's 'essential case': for a system dY/dz = A(z)Y with A an n×n matrix over ℚ(z), if for almost all primes p (all but finitely many, i.e. all p for which A can be reduced and the p-curvature A_p ≡ 0 mod p / the reduced system has a full set of solutions in 𝔽_p(z)) then the system has a full set (fundamental matrix, n independent solutions) of solutions algebraic over ℚ(z); only the sufficiency direction is conjectural (necessity is classical), the 'almost all p' quantifier must be cofinite not merely infinite, and the article notes the version for algebraic functions/number-field coefficients (Chambert-Loir's form for integrable connections on smooth varieties over a number field with an étale cover trivializing E) reduces to this case, so it is the same question rather than a separate variant.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the essential case (A ∈ M_n(ℚ(z)), cofinitely many primes, A_p ≡ 0 mod p or a fundamental matrix over 𝔽_p(z), conclusion an invertible fundamental matrix in an algebraic differential extension of ℚ(z)) in mathematically equivalent, faithful ways; I verified the recurrence A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A and the Cartier equivalences against Chambert-Loir §3. c04 was chosen as the base because it is the most Mathlib-idiomatic: d/dz is packaged as a `Differential (RatFunc K)` instance with proven quotient rule/additivity/Leibniz, the derivation on the finite extension L is Mathlib's canonical unique extension (`Differential.differentialFiniteDimensional`, confirmed by `rfl` and `DifferentialAlgebra F L` via inferInstance), the hypothesis explicitly includes p-integrality of A (so 'the reduced system' is meaningful pointwise, not just cofinitely as in c02), 'almost all p' is `∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, p.Prime → …`, and the bespoke definitions carry API/test lemmas as CONTRIBUTING.md asks. Edits: removed c04's extra `variants.necessity` (research solved) declaration since it is not a slot in the table, updated the docstring accordingly, corrected the Chambert-Loir section reference (§3, not §6), added AMS 34 (ODE), and wrapped three over-long lines. Boundary check: n = 0 makes hypothesis and conclusion both trivially true (consistent); hypothesis is satisfiable (A = 0); conclusion requires det Y ≠ 0 via IsUnit over a field, so it is not trivially satisfiable.

claims.decomposer_note: Katz's reformulation (Katz 1982, Conj. 9.2, stated in both cited arXiv papers): for a ℚ(x)-vector space M with connection ∇, the Lie algebra of the generic (Tannakian) differential Galois group Gal(M) ⊆ GL(M) equals the smallest algebraic Lie subalgebra of End_{ℚ(x)}(M) whose reduction mod p contains the p-curvature ψ_p = ∇(d/dx)^p for almost all p; the sources say this is equivalent to Grothendieck's conjecture (Grothendieck's for all connections implies Katz's), so it is an equivalent reformulation/generalization, subordinate to the primary slot; Farb–Kisin's proved cases, Schwarz's list and Di Vizio's proven q-analogue are progress/history, not questions posed.
claims.reviewer_why: Omitted. All eight candidates independently reported missing_primitives, and I agree: Katz's Conj. 9.2 (as quoted in Di Vizio's introduction) needs the generic Tannakian differential Galois group Gal(M) as an algebraic subgroup of GL(M) over ℚ(x) (stabilizer of all horizontal subquotients of mixed tensor constructions), the Lie algebra of an algebraic group, the notion of 'algebraic Lie subalgebra' of End(M), and reduction modulo p of such Lie subalgebras via a spreading-out lattice. Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have none of these (grep for PicardVessiot / differential Galois / AlgebraicGroup returns nothing). Any bespoke stand-in (e.g. an arbitrary LieSubalgebra) would state a different theorem, so it is better omitted than approximated. Since the sources say it is equivalent to Grothendieck's conjecture, no information about the open problem is lost.

context:
In mathematics, the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture is a local-global principle for linear ordinary differential equations, related to differential Galois theory and in a loose sense analogous to the result in the Chebotarev density theorem considered as the polynomial case. It is a conjecture of Alexander Grothendieck from the late 1960s, and apparently not published by him in any form.
The general case remains unsolved, despite recent progress; it has been linked to geometric investigations involving algebraic foliations.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture

A conjectured local–global principle for linear ordinary differential equations: a linear
differential system $dY/dz = A(z)\,Y$ with $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$ has a full set of algebraic
solutions as soon as, for all but finitely many primes $p$, its reduction modulo $p$ has
$p$-curvature zero (equivalently, has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$).

The $p$-curvature is computed by the recurrence $A_0 = I$, $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$ (so that
$d^kY/dz^k = A_k Y$ for every solution $Y$): the $p$-curvature of the reduction modulo $p$ vanishes
if and only if $A_p \equiv 0 \pmod p$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck%E2%80%93Katz_p-curvature_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. Chambert-Loir, *Théorèmes d'algébrisation en géométrie diophantienne*, Séminaire Bourbaki
  Exp. 886, §3, [arXiv:math/0103192](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103192)
- N. M. Katz, *Algebraic solutions of differential equations ($p$-curvature and the Hodge
  filtration)*, Invent. Math. 18 (1972), 1–118
- N. M. Katz, *A conjecture in the arithmetic theory of differential equations*, Bull. Soc. Math.
  France 110 (1982), 203–239
- L. Di Vizio, *Arithmetic theory of $q$-difference equations*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002),
  [arXiv:math/0104178](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0104178)
-/

namespace GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

open Polynomial RatFunc
open scoped Differential

/- ### The differential field `K(X)`

Mathlib has no derivation on `RatFunc K`. We define `d/dX` by the quotient rule on the reduced
numerator and denominator and record it as a `Differential` instance, so that the unique extension
of `d/dX` to finite extensions of `K(X)` (`Differential.differentialFiniteDimensional`) is
available. -/

section RatFuncDerivative

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- The derivative `d/dX` of a rational function `r = f / g` (with `f = r.num`, `g = r.denom`),
given by the quotient rule `(f' g - f g') / g ^ 2`. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivative (r : RatFunc K) : RatFunc K :=
  (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative r.num) * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.denom -
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.num * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative r.denom)) /
    algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.denom ^ 2

/-- The quotient rule holds for any representation `p / q` of a rational function, not only for
the reduced one. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem ratFuncDerivative_div (p q : K[X]) (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    ratFuncDerivative (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q) =
      (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative p) * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q -
          algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative q)) /
        algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q ^ 2 := by
  set r := algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q with hr
  have h1 : r.num * q = p * r.denom := (num_mul_eq_mul_denom_iff hq).mpr hr
  have h2 : derivative r.num * q + r.num * derivative q =
      derivative p * r.denom + p * derivative r.denom := by
    simpa only [derivative_mul] using congrArg derivative h1
  have key : (derivative r.num * r.denom - r.num * derivative r.denom) * q ^ 2 =
      (derivative p * q - p * derivative q) * r.denom ^ 2 := by
    linear_combination (r.denom * q) * h2 - (derivative q * r.denom + derivative r.denom * q) * h1
  unfold ratFuncDerivative
  rw [div_eq_div_iff (pow_ne_zero 2 (algebraMap_ne_zero (denom_ne_zero r)))
    (pow_ne_zero 2 (algebraMap_ne_zero hq))]
  simpa only [map_mul, map_sub, map_pow] using congrArg (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)) key

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem ratFuncDerivative_add (x y : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncDerivative (x + y) = ratFuncDerivative x + ratFuncDerivative y := by
  induction x using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₁ q₁ hq₁ => ?_
  induction y using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₂ q₂ hq₂ => ?_
  rw [div_add_div _ _ (algebraMap_ne_zero hq₁) (algebraMap_ne_zero hq₂), ← map_mul,
    ← map_mul, ← map_add, ← map_mul, ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ (mul_ne_zero hq₁ hq₂),
    ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₁, ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₂]
  have h₁ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₁
  have h₂ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₂
  simp only [derivative_mul, map_add, map_mul]
  field_simp
  ring

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem ratFuncDerivative_mul (x y : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncDerivative (x * y) = x * ratFuncDerivative y + y * ratFuncDerivative x := by
  induction x using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₁ q₁ hq₁ => ?_
  induction y using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₂ q₂ hq₂ => ?_
  rw [div_mul_div_comm, ← map_mul, ← map_mul,
    ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ (mul_ne_zero hq₁ hq₂), ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₁,
    ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₂]
  have h₁ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₁
  have h₂ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₂
  simp only [derivative_mul, map_add, map_mul]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- `ratFuncDerivative` as an additive map. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivativeAddHom : RatFunc K →+ RatFunc K :=
  AddMonoidHom.mk' ratFuncDerivative ratFuncDerivative_add

/-- The field `K(X)` of rational functions is a differential field for the derivation `d/dX`. -/
noncomputable instance : Differential (RatFunc K) where
  deriv := @Derivation.mk' ℤ _ (RatFunc K) _ (Ring.toIntAlgebra _) (RatFunc K) _ _ _
    (ratFuncDerivativeAddHom (K := K)).toIntLinearMap ratFuncDerivative_mul

/-- On polynomials, the derivation of `K(X)` is the usual polynomial derivative. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem deriv_algebraMap_polynomial (f : K[X]) :
    (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) f)′ = algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative f) := by
  change ratFuncDerivative _ = _
  simpa using ratFuncDerivative_div f 1 one_ne_zero

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem deriv_X : (X : RatFunc K)′ = 1 := by
  rw [← algebraMap_X, deriv_algebraMap_polynomial, derivative_X, map_one]

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem deriv_C (a : K) : (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (C a))′ = 0 := by
  rw [deriv_algebraMap_polynomial, derivative_C, map_zero]

end RatFuncDerivative

/- ### The matrices `A_k` and the `p`-curvature -/

section HigherDerivMatrix

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Differential R] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

/-- For a matrix `A` over a differential ring, `higherDerivMatrix A k` is the matrix `A_k` defined
by the recurrence `A_0 = 1`, `A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A` (where `A_k'` is the entrywise derivative),
so that every solution `Y` of `Y' = A Y` satisfies `Y^{(k)} = A_k Y`.

For `A` over `ℚ(z)` and a prime `p`, the reduction modulo `p` of `A_p` is the `p`-curvature of
the reduction modulo `p` of the system `Y' = A Y`. -/
noncomputable def higherDerivMatrix (A : Matrix ι ι R) : ℕ → Matrix ι ι R
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => (higherDerivMatrix A k).map (·′) + higherDerivMatrix A k * A

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem higherDerivMatrix_zero (A : Matrix ι ι R) : higherDerivMatrix A 0 = 1 := rfl

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem higherDerivMatrix_succ (A : Matrix ι ι R) (k : ℕ) :
    higherDerivMatrix A (k + 1) =
      (higherDerivMatrix A k).map (·′) + higherDerivMatrix A k * A := rfl

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem higherDerivMatrix_one (A : Matrix ι ι R) : higherDerivMatrix A 1 = A := by
  have : (1 : Matrix ι ι R).map (·′) = 0 := by
    ext i j
    by_cases h : i = j <;> simp [h]
  simp [higherDerivMatrix, this]

end HigherDerivMatrix

/- ### Reduction modulo `p` of rational functions over `ℚ` -/

section ReductionModP

/-- A rational function `r ∈ ℚ(z)` is *`p`-integral* (its reduction modulo `p` is defined) if
`r = f / g` with `f, g ∈ ℤ[z]` and `g ≢ 0 (mod p)`. Equivalently, `r` has `p`-adic Gauss norm
at most `1`. -/
def IsPIntegral (p : ℕ) (r : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f g : ℤ[X], g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    r = algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (f.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) /
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))

/-- A rational function `r ∈ ℚ(z)` is *zero modulo `p`* if `r = f / g` with `f, g ∈ ℤ[z]`,
`g ≢ 0 (mod p)` and `f ≡ 0 (mod p)`. Equivalently, `r` has `p`-adic Gauss norm less than `1`,
i.e. `r` is `p`-integral and its reduction in `𝔽_p(z)` is `0`. -/
def IsZeroModP (p : ℕ) (r : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f g : ℤ[X], g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    f.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = 0 ∧
    r = algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (f.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) /
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem isZeroModP_zero (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : IsZeroModP p 0 :=
  ⟨0, 1, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_isZeroModP_one (p : ℕ) : ¬ IsZeroModP p 1 := by
  rintro ⟨f, g, hg, hf, h⟩
  have hg' : g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    rintro hg'
    simp [hg'] at h
  rw [eq_div_iff (algebraMap_ne_zero hg'), one_mul] at h
  have hfg : f = g := Polynomial.map_injective _ (Int.castRingHom ℚ).injective_int
    (algebraMap_injective ℚ h).symm
  exact hg (hfg ▸ hf)

/-- The linear differential system `Y' = A Y`, for `A` an `n × n` matrix over `ℚ(z)`, has
*`p`-curvature zero modulo `p`*: `A` can be reduced modulo `p` (all its entries are `p`-integral)
and the `p`-curvature matrix `A_p` of the reduction is zero, i.e. `A_p ≡ 0 (mod p)` entrywise.
By a theorem of Cartier, this holds if and only if the reduction modulo `p` of the system has a
full set of solutions in `𝔽_p(z)` (equivalently, of solutions algebraic over `𝔽_p(z)`). -/
def HasPCurvatureZero {n : ℕ} (p : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j, IsPIntegral p (A i j)) ∧ ∀ i j, IsZeroModP p (higherDerivMatrix A p i j)

end ReductionModP

/- ### Full sets of algebraic solutions -/

section AlgebraicSolutions

variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Differential F] [CharZero F]

/-- The linear differential system `Y' = A Y`, for `A` an `n × n` matrix over a differential
field `F` of characteristic `0`, has a *full set of algebraic solutions*: there is a fundamental
matrix of solutions, i.e. an invertible `n × n` matrix `Y` with `Y' = A Y`, whose entries lie in
a finite extension `L` of `F` (inside an algebraic closure of `F`). Here `L` carries the unique
derivation extending that of `F`. -/
def HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : IntermediateField F (AlgebraicClosure F)) (_ : FiniteDimensional F L)
    (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L),
    IsUnit Y ∧ Y.map (·′) = A.map (algebraMap F L) * Y

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem hasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions_zero (n : ℕ) :
    HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions (0 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F) :=
  ⟨⊥, inferInstance, 1, isUnit_one, by
    ext i j
    by_cases h : i = j <;> simp [h]⟩

end AlgebraicSolutions

/-- **Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture** (Grothendieck's conjecture, in its essential
case). Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix of rational functions in $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, and consider
the linear differential system $dY/dz = A(z)\,Y$. Let $A_0 = I$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$, so
that $d^kY/dz^k = A_k Y$ for every solution $Y$.

Suppose that for all but finitely many primes $p$, the system can be reduced modulo $p$ and the
reduced system has $p$-curvature zero, i.e. $A_p \equiv 0 \pmod p$ (equivalently, the reduced
system has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$, or algebraic over $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$).
Then the system has a full set of algebraic solutions: a fundamental matrix
$Y \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ with $Y' = AY$, whose entries lie in a finite extension $L$ of
$\mathbb{Q}(z)$.

Only this sufficiency direction is conjectural; the converse (necessity of the mod $p$ condition)
is a classical theorem of Cartier and Katz. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 12 14 34]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (hA : ∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, p.Prime → HasPCurvatureZero p A) :
    HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions A := by
  sorry

end GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

items: The list-page entry is terse, so the statement was taken from the article's 'essential case' (rational-function matrix A over ℚ(z), rational coefficients), as the notes prescribe; the number-field/étale-cover version (Chambert-Loir's Conj.) is treated as the same question and not stated separately.

ℚ(z) is modelled as `RatFunc ℚ`. Mathlib has no derivation on RatFunc, so `d/dz` is defined by the quotient rule on num/denom, proven to satisfy the quotient rule for every representation p/q (`ratFuncDerivative_div`), additivity and Leibniz, and packaged as a `Differential (RatFunc K)` instance; `deriv_algebraMap_polynomial`, `deriv_X`, `deriv_C` check it agrees with `Polynomial.derivative`. This instance is reusable and would belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib in a real PR.

The mod-p condition is encoded via the matrices A_k of Chambert-Loir (A_0 = I, A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A, column convention dY/dz = A Y matching Wikipedia's dv/dz = A(z)v): `HasPCurvatureZero p A` := all entries of A are p-integral (A can be reduced mod p) ∧ all entries of A_p are ≡ 0 mod p. By Cartier's theorem (quoted in Chambert-Loir) this is exactly 'the reduction mod p has a full set of solutions in 𝔽_p(z) / algebraic over 𝔽_p(z)'. Including the reducibility clause is harmless under the cofinite quantifier and matches the source's 'si l'on peut réduire A modulo p'.

`IsPIntegral p r` (r = f/g, f,g ∈ ℤ[z], g ≢ 0 mod p) and `IsZeroModP p r` (additionally f ≡ 0 mod p) are elementary encodings of 'p-adic Gauss norm ≤ 1' and '< 1'; by Gauss's lemma they are representation-independent and equal to 'reducible mod p' and 'reduces to 0 in 𝔽_p(z)'. Congruences of ℤ[z] are expressed via `Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p))`.
'Almost all primes' is `∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, p.Prime → …`, i.e. all but finitely many primes (cofinite, not merely infinitely many), as the notes require.

'Full set of algebraic solutions' = a fundamental matrix: `∃ L : IntermediateField F (AlgebraicClosure F)` finite-dimensional over F, `∃ Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L`, `IsUnit Y ∧ Y.map (·′) = A.map (algebraMap F L) * Y`. The derivation on L is Mathlib's `Differential.instSubtypeMemIntermediateFieldOfFiniteDimensional` (verified by #synth), the unique extension of the derivation of F (`uniqueDifferentialAlgebraFiniteDimensional`). Any finite set of algebraic elements lies in such an L, so this is equivalent to 'n independent solutions algebraic over ℚ(z)'. The predicate is stated for a general differential field F of characteristic 0 (instantiated at F = RatFunc ℚ) to avoid a RatFunc-specific typeclass-search blow-up.

Only the sufficiency direction is the open conjecture (`research open`). The classical necessity (Cartier/Katz 1970–72) is added as `grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture.variants.necessity` tagged `research solved` with `sorry`, both to document that only one direction is conjectural and to exercise the definitions; a reviewer should confirm they want this extra declaration.
Index type is `Fin n` (n×n matrices); n = 0 makes both hypothesis and conclusion trivially true, which is consistent.
AMS tags 11 12 14 (arithmetic of differential equations, differential algebra, algebraic geometry).

reviewer_notes: The list-page statement is a one-line description; the precise formulation was taken from the Wikipedia article's 'essential case' together with Chambert-Loir §3 (arXiv:math/0103192) and Di Vizio's introduction (arXiv:math/0104178), as the decomposition notes prescribe. Modeling notes for reviewers: (1) the mod-p hypothesis is encoded via the p-curvature matrix A_p computed over ℚ(z) and then reduced (A p-integral ∧ A_p ≡ 0 mod p); reduction commutes with d/dz on p-integral rational functions, and by Cartier's theorem this is exactly 'the reduced system has a full set of solutions in 𝔽_p(z)'; (2) 'full set of algebraic solutions' is an invertible fundamental matrix Y with Y' = AY over a finite-dimensional intermediate field of the algebraic closure of ℚ(z), carrying Mathlib's unique extension of the derivation — finite vs. algebraic extension is immaterial, and this matches Chambert-Loir's 'local holomorphic solutions algebraic over ℚ(z)' by the usual embedding argument; (3) 'almost all p' is the cofinite filter (all but finitely many primes), not 'infinitely many'; (4) only the conjectural sufficiency direction is stated. The reusable derivation section (`ratFuncDerivative`, `Differential (RatFunc K)` instance, `higherDerivMatrix`) would belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib in a real PR but is kept in the single problem file here as required by the task. c04's `variants.necessity` (classical converse, research solved) was faithful but dropped because it is not a slot in the table; c02 also had such a variant. All candidates' omission of the Katz slot is judged correct.
